r: Slave bought by Iltutmish → **water-carrier** → member of **the Forty** → **Amir-i-Shikar** (under Razia) → **naib** (principal minister) of **Nasiruddin Mahmud**, who gave him the title **Ulugh Khan**
Leader of the **Indian Muslim** group who briefly displaced Balban in Nasiruddin Mahmud's reign
Copied the **Iranian kings**; strict etiquette, aloofness
Broke **the Forty** by promoting **junior Turks**; efficient spies; harsh justice
Amir **Malik Baqbaq** (governor of Badaun) **publicly flogged** for killing a servant
Created the military department **Diwan-i-Arz**, separate from the **Diwan-i-Wizarat** (finance); **outposts and forts** against the Mongols
Moved from **Lahore to Delhi** – first Sultan to make **Delhi** the capital and issue **regular coins**
Purely **Arabic** silver **tanka** and copper **jital** – basis of the later rupee

**Chengiz (Genghis) Khan** – original name **Temujin (Temuchin)** – reached the **Indus (1221)** chasing **Jalaluddin Mangbarni** of Khwarazm; Iltutmish **refused him shelter**, so the Mongols turned back – their first appearance on the Indus
**Tajuddin Yildiz** (beaten at **Tarain, 1216**); **Nasiruddin Qabacha** (Multan, Uch; fought for Lahore)
After defeating Iwaz Khalji of Bengal, made **Malik (Alauddin) Jani** the **first governor of Bihar**
"The Forty" – **Turkish military** elite (not Persian revenue clerks)
Revenue assignment to officers (**muqtis**) instead of cash salary

1.x: **Buildings:** completed the **Qutb Minar** (begun by Aibak; dedicated to **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**); **Sultan Ghari** tomb → "**Father of tomb building**".

2.x: **Origin:** born in **Turkestan**; sold to the **Qazi of Nishapur**, then slave of **Muhammad Ghori**; **Amir-i-Akhur** (Master of Stables) → general; Ghori's representative after **Tarain II (1192)**.
**Titles:** **Lakh Bakhsh** ("giver of lakhs"); **Quran Khwan / "Quran Khan"** (reciter of the Quran).
**Buildings:** began the **Qutb Minar**; **Quwwat-ul-Islam** mosque (first mosque in Delhi); **Adhai Din ka Jhonpra** (Ajmer).
**Death (1210):** at **Lahore** – **fell from his horse while playing chaugan (polo)**; buried near **Anarkali Bazaar**.

3.x: **Status:** **First and only woman ruler** of the Delhi Sultanate – the first woman ruler of medieval India, before Chand Bibi, Durgavati, Nur Jahan.
**Ways:** discarded **purdah**, wore **male attire** (kuba, kulah), hunted, led the army.
**Opposition:** the **Turkish nobles** (the Forty) resented her favour to **Yaqut**, an **Abyssinian** (Amir-i-Akhur) → her fall.
**1240:** **Altuniya**, governor of **Bhatinda (Tabarhinda)**, revolted → Yaqut killed, Razia imprisoned; she **married Altuniya**, marched on Delhi and was **killed**.

r: Arabic "**owned**" – an owned **military slave**; Slave dynasty ruled **1206-1290**
Most amirs and Sultans of the Sultanate were **Turks** (Turko-Afghan)

4.x: **Order:** Aibak → Aram Shah → **Iltutmish** → **Ruknuddin Firuz** → **Razia** → Bahram Shah → Masud → **Nasiruddin Mahmud** (1246-66; Tabaqat-i-Nasiri named after him) → **Balban** → **Kaiqubad** → infant **Kaimurs** (last).
**End:** **Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji** – a Khalji, not a Mamluk – crowned himself at **Kilokhari (1290)** → **Khalji** dynasty.
